We have our first quiz in just a couple of days - on Wednesday, October 21st. The problems on the quiz will be a subset of variations of these problems.

## Problems 

1. Write down the following definitions

   a. Convergent series  
   [Definition 4.1.12 ](https://complexanalysis.org/web/sec_sequences-series.html#sec_sequences-series-27){target=_blank} of our text  
   b. Absolute convergent series  
   [Definition 4.1.13 ](https://complexanalysis.org/web/sec_sequences-series.html#sec_sequences-series-28){target=_blank} of our text


2. Find the largest open disks on which each of the following series converges:

   a. $\displaystyle \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{n^2}{n!} z^n$
   <div style="height:10px"></div>
   \vspace{2mm}
   b. $\displaystyle \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{n^3}{3^n} (z-(4+3i))^n$

   Note that degenerate cases, such as a single point or all of $\mathbb{C}$ are possible.

3. Use the geometric series formula to evaluate the following series:

   a. $\displaystyle \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{1}{(1+i)^n}$
   <div style="height:10px"></div>
   \vspace{2mm}
   b. $\displaystyle \sum_{n=3}^{\infty} \frac{2^{n+2}}{(3+4i)^n}$

4. Starting with the series representation
$$
\arctan(z) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} (-1)^n \frac{z^{2 n+1}}{2 n+1},
$$
find a power series representation of 
$$
\int \arctan(z^2) \, dz.
$$
What is the largest open disk on which your power series is valid?

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
